holidays.name: National Chocolate Cake Day
holidays.description: A day for treating yourself to a slice of rich, fudgy chocolate cake. Frosting is welcome, and seconds are encouraged. Birthday-party staple, midnight-snack hero, and dessert-table showstopper all in one.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a favorite on the American food-holiday calendar.
holidays.funFact: Chocolate was a drink for most of its history. The first chocolate cakes only appeared in the 18th century, and the dense, fudgy kind we know today came much later.

holidays.name: Thomas Crapper Day
holidays.description: A cheeky tribute to the famed Victorian plumber and sanitary engineer whose name became forever tied to the loo. Celebrate by appreciating indoor plumbing, flushing with gratitude, and swapping bathroom puns.
holidays.origin: The day marks the anniversary of Thomas Crapper's death on January 27, 1910. He ran a well-known plumbing business in London.
holidays.funFact: Crapper didn't invent the flush toilet, despite the popular myth. He did hold several plumbing-related patents and made showrooms for bathroom fixtures a respectable business.

holidays.name: Punch the Clock Day
holidays.description: A salute to the humble time clock and the inventors who made tracking work hours fair and precise. It's a good day to clock in on time, or at least to feel nostalgic about the satisfying thunk of a punch card.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance, linked to the history of time-recording devices for workers.
holidays.funFact: Mechanical time recorders for workers appeared in the late 1800s. Companies that made them eventually merged into the firm that became IBM.
